sections.html:
Christian County sits in the Ozarks between Springfield and Branson. Ozark holds the courthouse and Nixa has the most residents. The county keeps adding people, from 88,842 at the 2020 census to an estimated 96,725 in mid-2025. About three homes in four (75.9%) are lived in by their owners, so a listing here usually competes with other owner-occupied houses and with new builds.

  • The county had 38,594 housing units in 2025 and builders pulled 495 permits that year.
  • The 2020 to 2024 middle value for an owner-occupied home was $274,900.
  • Median household income is $83,437.

Two offices matter for tax, and both work out of the historic courthouse on the Ozark square. The Assessor decides value. The Collector of Revenue sends the statements.

• Collector of Revenue: 100 W. Church, Room 101, Ozark, MO 65721, (417) 582-4330. Weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:30, and the counter stays open at lunch.
  • Assessor: real estate questions at 417-582-4310, personal property at 417-582-4320.
  • Payment options include the counter, the mail, christiancountycollector.com, the toll-free number printed on the bill, and a drop box on the west side of the courthouse that is available around the clock.

The Collector collects what the Assessor's records say and has no power to change a statement. If the mailing address, vehicle list or legal description is wrong, fix it with the Assessor first. The office refuses partial payments and wrong amounts.

The 2026 statements went into the mail in early November. You can pay the day one arrives, and the balance turns delinquent after December 31. Mail must be postmarked 12/31/26 by the USPS, and the website stops taking payments at 11:59 p.m. that evening. A glitch on the phone line or website buys no extra time, the Collector says. If you escrow through a lender, confirm the lender has paid before the end of the year.

Owners in four small towns can pay close to home. Collector staff set up from 9 a.m. to noon on specific days at the city halls in Billings, Clever, Sparta and Highlandville. Only cash, check or money order is taken there (no cards), with checks in blue or black ink. Carry the full statement, and call the office for the posted days.

No statement by the end of November means a phone call to the Collector. Mail that goes missing does not cancel the tax.

A processing charge is added on top of the tax for electronic payments. None of it goes to the county, and RSMo 139.055 lets the cost land only on those who pick the electronic route.

Way to payFee
E-check$2.00
Debit card$4.00
Credit card2.45 percent of the balance
Cash, personal check, cashier's check or money order at the office or drop boxNo fee

Clerks at the DMV and Department of Revenue accept a paid receipt shown on a phone.

The Assessor prices every taxable item in the county using its January 1 condition. Its roll holds more than 42,951 real estate parcels and over 38,457 personal property accounts, and total assessed value for 2025 tops $2 billion. State class rates turn market value into assessed value: residential 19 percent, commercial 32 percent, agricultural land 12 percent.

Value covers only part of the math. Each taxing district also sets a levy, and the Assessor tallies thirteen school districts, eight road districts, ten cities, nine fire districts and nine other districts for services like ambulance, senior programs and the junior college. Which of them overlap your parcel determines the total, so read the district names on your bill. The Assessor's page also hosts Value Change Notices, exemption applications and address change forms.

An owner who objects to a value can climb from the Assessor to a county board and finally the State Tax Commission. Under RSMo 137.275, the Board of Equalization must receive your appeal by the second Monday in July. If the board's answer is unsatisfactory, RSMo 138.430 allows a commission appeal within the chapter 138 deadline, or 30 days after the board's last action if that is later.

  • Study your Value Change Notice and compare it with the market data the Assessor posts.
  • Phone 417-582-4310 and request an informal review of the number.
  • Get the board's form and hearing dates from the County Clerk.
  • When assessed value climbed 15 percent or more, RSMo 138.060 the Assessor must carry the burden of proof, except where new construction caused the increase.

Strict rules govern the Senate Bill 190 senior citizen real estate tax credit, and both the county home page and the Assessor's page post them. An approved owner renews with no new paperwork as long as they still qualify and added no improvements. A spouse who has just reached the age must file an application.

  • First-time forms are available March 1, 2027, and the Collector's office in Room 101 takes them through June 15, 2027.
  • Applicants need to be 62 or older by midnight on December 31, 2026.
  • The house must lie in Christian County and have been the applicant's primary residence since at least June 29, 2026.
  • Pay the 2026 taxes, finish the personal property assessment and have each applicant's signature notarized.

sections.h2: Selling with a tax bill due
sections.html:
Whoever owns the property owes all the tax on it, and the obligation is fixed as of January 1. Your title company can explain how the closing statement splits the year. Ask the Collector for the exact balance ahead of closing day.

Here is a workable order of operations. First, find your newest statement and jot down the parcel number and taxing districts. Second, get a written payoff figure from the Collector. Third, let the title company pay whatever is owed from your proceeds. Fourth, once the deed records, send the Collector and Assessor the buyer's name and mailing address so the next bill goes out correctly. Cash Home Buyers can close without a lender in the middle, which helps when a house carries back taxes or needs work, and the closing agent still settles the tax line.

faqs.q: By what date must 2026 Christian County taxes be paid?
faqs.a: Pay by December 31, 2026. Mail must be postmarked 12/31/26 and the website closes at 11:59 p.m. that night. After that the balance is delinquent, and problems with the phone or web system do not move the date.

faqs.q: Where do I pay in person?
faqs.a: Go to Room 101 at 100 W. Church in Ozark on a weekday between 8:00 and 4:30. The courthouse's west side has a drop box that never closes, and Billings, Clever, Sparta and Highlandville host city hall payment days.

faqs.q: What are the card fees on a tax payment?
faqs.a: A credit card costs 2.45 percent of the balance extra, a debit card $4.00 and an e-check $2.00. The county keeps none of it. Paying in person by cash, check or money order has no fee.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my home?
faqs.a: The Assessor does, using the January 1 condition and the state class rates of 19, 32 and 12 percent for residential, commercial and agricultural land. Real estate questions go to 417-582-4310. Each tax district then applies its own levy.

faqs.q: Can seniors reduce their tax bill?
faqs.a: Maybe, if you qualify for the SB 190 senior citizen real estate tax credit. New applications run March 1 to June 15, 2027, for owners who are 62 by December 31, 2026. Those already approved renew on their own.
